part.text:
All done. Summary of what was added:

- **`src/serve.ts`** — new `serve()` function: builds the site, starts an HTTP server on `dist/` (default port 3000), watches `content/` and `templates/` with chokidar, debounces rebuilds, and runs a WebSocket server (`ws`) on the same port at `/__livereload`. HTML responses get a live-reload `<script>` injected before `</body>`; a rebuild broadcasts `"reload"` to connected clients, which triggers `location.reload()`. Path traversal is blocked and non-HTML assets are served with proper MIME types. `ServeHandle` exposes `port`, `ready()`, and `close()`.
- **`src/cli.ts`** — added a `serve` command (with `--content`/`--output`/`--templates`/`--port`, default port 3000), while `build` behavior is untouched.
- **`package.json`** — added `chokidar`, `ws`, `@types/ws` deps and an `"serve": "ssg serve"` script.
- **`jest.config.js`** — pinned `maxWorkers: 1`: the real HTTP/WebSocket/file-watcher tests intermittently raced jest-worker's teardown timing under parallel workers (harmless but noisy); serial execution removed the flake entirely (verified over many repeated runs) and is still fast for this small suite.
- Tests added in `src/serve.test.ts` (build-on-start + injected script, static asset serving, 404, path-traversal rejection, real file-change → rebuild → WebSocket reload) and `src/cli.test.ts` (`--port` parsing, `serve` command end-to-end).
- Verified manually end-to-end via `node bin/ssg.js serve --port 3577`: served pages contained the live-reload script, and editing `content/about.md` triggered a real rebuild reflected in `dist/about.html`.
